title: UAE_Strategy_for_Artificial_Intelligence
summary:
The UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence is a national initiative launched by the United Arab Emirates in October 2017 as part of its broader UAE Centennial 2071 vision. It aims to position the UAE as a global leader in artificial intelligence by 2031, integrating AI technologies across various sectors.

The initiative has the following objectives: to build a reputation as an AI destination; to increase the UAE's competitive assets in priority sectors through the deployment of AI; to develop a fertile ecosystem for AI; to adopt AI across government services to improve lives; to attract and train talent for future jobs enabled by AI; to bring world-leading research capability to work with target industries; to provide the data and supporting infrastructure essential to become a test bed for AI; and to ensure strong governance and effective regulation. The strategy outlines an ambitious vision with the aim of generating AED 335 billion in economic growth.

Priority sectors for AI deployment include energy, logistics, tourism, healthcare, and cybersecurity. The UAE appointed the world's first Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence in 2017. Central to the AI investment drive is MGX, a $100 billion AI investment company launched by sovereign wealth fund Mubadala, investing in leading AI technologies and partnerships including data centers and energy infrastructure. Microsoft invested $1.5 billion in G42 and joined its board of directors, with collaboration including integrating Microsoft's Azure cloud services across the UAE.

The strategy places a strong emphasis on governance and regulation to ensure the responsible development of AI, with the UAE seeking to lead global discussions on AI governance. In 2022, the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence issued AI Ethics guidelines that include non-binding guidelines for developers and investors.
